operations.content: Personal financial dashboard built on a Finviz Elite subscription, for both real research/trading use and as a learning project. Local-only, single-user, no auth needed.

8-phase roadmap: 1) foundation + stock lookup, 2) screener, 3) options chain viewer (Schwab API), 4) watchlists + alerts, 5) options strategy suggestions, 6) insider/institutional feed, 7) news + sentiment, 8) portfolio tracking + backtesting. Order front-loads the two biggest unknowns (Finviz export API, Schwab API auth).

User is an experienced software engineer but new to financial/trading APIs. Wants domain-specific quirks (Finviz export semantics, options mechanics, market data behavior) documented in code/docs, but doesn't need general software engineering explained.
Backend: Python + FastAPI. Frontend: React + TypeScript (Vite). Chosen so pandas can handle Finviz's CSV-shaped export data and screener manipulation naturally.
SQLite for local persistence (response cache, later saved screens/watchlists/portfolio data). Chosen over Postgres since this is local-only single-user.
Docker Compose used for local dev (backend, frontend, SQLite volume as services), not plain local processes, per explicit user preference.
Finviz Elite export API (CSV endpoints at export.finviz.com, auth via static token in URL) for quotes/screener/fundamentals. Finviz has NO options data at all (no chains, IV, or greeks) on any tier.

Schwab developer API (user has a Schwab/thinkorswim brokerage account) will supply options chains and greeks. Requires a developer app approval process that can take days, so should be started early/in parallel.
Backend owns all external API calls (Finviz, Schwab); frontend never calls them directly. Keeps the Finviz Elite token and Schwab credentials server-side only, never shipped to the browser.

A finviz_client module wraps Finviz's CSV export endpoints and cryptic filter codes behind typed Python functions (get_quote(ticker), run_screener(filters)); rest of app never touches raw CSV/URL-encoding or Finviz filter codes directly.
Brainstorming/design phase complete for Phase 1 (foundation + stock lookup). Writing design spec doc next, then an implementation plan.

After phase 1 spec is approved: invoke writing-plans skill for the phase 1 implementation plan. Later phases (screener, options/Schwab, watchlists, etc.) each get their own brainstorm -> spec -> plan cycle.

operations.content: FAILED: assuming Finviz rejects bad filter codes -> unknown f=/s= codes are silently ignored and the export returns the whole market (~10,400 rows). INSTEAD: treat >5,000 rows as 'filters may have been ignored' and verify every code via the sanity script.

Finviz Elite bars: quote_export.ashx?t=X&p=d gives ~10y daily; p=i1 ~2 weeks of 1m and p=i5 ~3 weeks of 5m, 04:00-20:00 ET incl. extended hours. Intraday timestamps look like '10/20/2026 19:59 PM' (24h clock + redundant AM/PM). Massive (Polygon) is the fallback for deeper intraday history.

Finviz wide export v=152&c=<ids> returns columns in ascending id order (map by header name), accepts many comma-separated tickers in t=, Market Cap/Shares Float in millions, Average Volume in thousands. Useful ids: float 25, rel vol 64, change 66, AH change 72, news title 137.

User trades small-cap momentum (US, under $20, float <10-20M, rel vol 2x+, top gainers, after-hours), long only today but plans to short later. Workflow: screen -> news -> 2y daily S/R lines -> 1m/5m reaction. Wants pattern detection, long/short verdict, entry/exit at 3:1 R:R, ranked.

operations.content: FAILED: assuming a bad Finviz filter code returns the whole market, so big results = typo -> Finviz drops each unknown f=/s= code individually and applies the rest (no error); valid broad screens exceed 5,000 rows (US only 10,435; market 11,758). INSTEAD: test each code alone vs the no-filter count (app: find_unrecognised_codes at screen save).

Finviz export can answer HTTP 200 with an HTML page or empty body; requests exception messages embed the URL incl. auth token. finviz_client therefore checks for a Ticker column, wraps parse errors as FinvizUnavailableError, and raises its errors 'from None' so the token never reaches logs.

Docker may be unavailable from WSL (Docker Desktop integration off) and port 5173 is often taken by another project's vite. Smoke-test instead with backend/.venv uvicorn --port 8000 (DB_PATH in scratchpad, env from .env) plus 'npx vite --port 5174 --strictPort'.

FAILED: kill $(pgrep -f '<pattern>') to stop a background server -> also matched and killed the invoking bash shell. INSTEAD: get the PID from 'ss -ltnp' on the port, or pgrep -f with a pattern anchored to the binary path, and check the list before killing.

operations.content: Pattern-detector fixtures that start at 9:30 hide real-data bugs: Finviz intraday bars begin at 04:00 ET, so 'today' includes pre-market.
